exposure: PPA (Adequate Childbirth Project) quality improvement intervention
outcome: absence of antibiotic prophylaxis in Group B Streptococcus (GBS)+ women
absence of antibiotic prophylaxis for CSs
not receiving magnesium sulphate in severe hypertension
obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) following an episiotomy
requiring antibiotics other than routine prophylaxis
cohort: The study included 4789 births from women in 12 private hospitals in Brazil, divided into a group exposed to the PPA intervention and a group receiving standard care.
finding: The PPA intervention successfully reduced cesarean section rates, late preterm, and early term deliveries without increasing the chance of adverse outcomes.
mod_finding: The PPA intervention significantly reduced overall, prelabor, and repeated cesarean section rates.
